entities.summary: Richard Trevithick was a British inventor and mining engineer. The son of a mining captain, and born in the mining heartland of Cornwall, Trevithick was immersed in mining and engineering from an early age. He was an early pioneer of steam-powered road and rail transport, and his most significant contributions were the development of the first high-pressure steam engine and the first working railway steam locomotive. The world's first locomotive-hauled railway journey took place on 21 February 1804, when Trevithick's unnamed steam locomotive hauled a train along the tramway of the Penydarren Ironworks, in Merthyr Tydfil, Wales.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Trevithick's development of the first high-pressure steam engine and the first working railway steam locomotive marked a pivotal moment in the Industrial Revolution, enabling mass transportation and transforming global trade and commerce. His achievement on February 21, 1804, at the Penydarren Ironworks, was a precursor to the widespread adoption of steam power in railways across Europe and North America.
